lines.text: Imagine this.
An earthquake strikes and a building is severely damaged.
People are trapped inside.
But nobody knows where they are.
Rescue teams arrive. They need to find those people, and they need to find them FAST.
But there's a problem.
Nobody knows what's inside.
And every second spent searching could mean a life lost.
Today, rescue teams use a big, bulky, specialized drone to search dangerous buildings.
But mapping an entire building with just one drone is SLOW,
these drones are EXPENSIVE,
and teams often have just ONE or TWO available.
It also takes time that victims do not have.
So we asked ourselves...
What if we could search an ENTIRE building... in a fraction of the time?
Not with ONE drone.
Not with TWO.
But with an ENTIRE SWARM of small, affordable drones that FLY THEMSELVES!
Introducing SWARM!
Our swarm spreads out, searching different parts of the building AT THE SAME TIME!
No need for someone to fly each drone.
And everything they see comes together into ONE LIVE 3D MAP!
It shows rescuers where people are trapped,
in fact, it tracks their vitals using Presage,
it shows where paths are blocked,
and where danger lies.
Here's what changes. We now have:
FASTER SEARCHES! Because many drones explore at once.
LOWER COSTS! Because we use small, affordable drones sharing one powerful computer.
AND NO PILOT FOR EVERY DRONE! Because they are autonomous.
And research backs this up!
A 2024 study published in Sensors found that collaborative robots reduced indoor mapping time by nearly 50%!
On the other hand, specialized drones can cost way up to $30,000 EACH!
But enough talking. Let's dive into the demonstration!
We've turned this idea into a platform designed to make search-and-rescue operations faster, safer, and smarter.
From sending out autonomous drones to tracking their progress, everything is designed to help rescue teams act quickly.
And the best part? Rescuers can manage everything from one place.
So, let's see it in action!
First, we select the building and the type of emergency.
And with one click, we launch our FOUR autonomous drones!
Now, this is where the rescue team monitors the entire mission!
Here, you can see all four drones exploring different parts of the building AT THE SAME TIME!
And everything they see comes together into ONE live 3D map, showing the building's layout and how much we've explored!
And look! We've detected a potential survivor!
We can even see their estimated breathing rate and pulse using Presage!
As we scroll, we can also see dangers detected along the way, like blocked passages, closed doors, and gas cylinders!
And here's the best part!
We can send this information directly to the rescue crew, helping them decide where to go!
But how does all of this work behind the scenes?
Here's our technical team to explain!
Each drone is a cheap E58 quadcopter. An ESP32-S3 relay streams its camera over Wi-Fi to one GPU computer.
Our Rust and CUDA core fuses every view into one shared 3D map, and plans each drone's next move.
YOLO26 spots people, doors and fire.
It all syncs through SpacetimeDB to the console. The full swarm runs in our simulator; our real drone streams live today.
Next: real swarm flights, and robots like Boston Dynamics Spot.
When lives are on the line...
EVERY SECOND COUNTS!
SWARM. SEND THE SWARM!
